origin: Credited to William Playfair, who first drew one in 1801. It means slicing a circle like a pie.
whenToUse: There are two to four items that add up to 100%.
You show a big difference, such as whether one item is more than half.
There's no need for a number in the middle.
whenNotToUse: There are more than five items (use a bar chart).
Showing the total in the middle (use a donut chart).

alternatives.name: Donut Chart
alternatives.reason: Showing the total in the middle.

alternatives.name: Stacked Bar Chart
alternatives.reason: Viewing the composition of several periods side by side.

accessibility: Legend items are buttons, so Tab moves through them and highlights each slice.
The legend writes values and percentages, so it reads without the slices.
A 2px white line between slices keeps edges visible even with similar colors.
